subject: Scheduling: technical deep dive on serving runtime, KV cache & quantization
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@nebulah.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@nebulah.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: deep dive on serving runtime for Nebula Health POC

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profiles. Nebula's platform team would like a follow-up technical deep dive focused on your serving runtime architecture, specifically:

- KV cache behavior during long chat sessions
- Quantization fallbacks and memory tradeoffs
- Batching strategy for mixed short/long requests

Could we schedule a 60–75 minute session next week with your infra/serving folks (including an architecture walkthrough, sequence diagrams, and space for Q&A)? Prefer mornings PST.

Attendees on our side: myself (platform lead), and two engineers from the infra team (platform@nebulah.com).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Platform Lead, Nebula Health
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@nebulah.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deep dive on serving runtime for Nebula Health POC

Hi Alice — great to hear. We're excited to do a focused technical session. Proposed options (all 60 min slots, we can extend to 75 if needed):

- Tue 2026-05-25 09:00–10:00 PT
- Wed 2026-05-26 10:00–11:00 PT
- Thu 2026-05-27 08:30–09:30 PT

Proposed agenda (high-level):
1) 5 min — goals and success criteria (Nebula + Redwood)
2) 20 min — runtime architecture walkthrough (serving nodes, kernel selection, quantization paths)
3) 20 min — KV cache & long-session behaviour (design, cache eviction, prefix caching) + sequence diagrams
4) 10–15 min — batching strategies / autoscaling considerations + Q&A

Pre-reads: I've uploaded a short runtime overview and the current sequence diagrams to Drive (links below). We'll attach a PDF of the 10-slide runtime overview to the invite.

Attachments (preview):
- ri-runtime-overview-v1.pdf (10 slides)
- kv-cache-seq-diagram.png (sequence diagram)
- deepdive-agenda-v2.pdf (one-page agenda)

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRI-runtime-prereads | https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFR/DEAL-4521+Nebula+Health+Integration

Jonas (serving runtime lead) and Rishi (platform infra) are copied — Jonas will run the live walkthrough. Any specific sections you want us to expand? Also confirm preferred slot from the options above.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@nebulah.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deep dive on serving runtime for Nebula Health POC

Hi Alice — thanks for organizing. Quick note on what I'll cover and a small ask:

I'll step through the runtime topology (worker pools, KV cache lookups, CPU/GPU kernel routing). For the KV cache section I'd like to show the sequence diagram (kv-cache-seq-diagram.png) and a short trace example. If Nebula can share an anonymized example of a long-chat trace (or a sequence length distribution), we can tailor the caching discussion.

Also: if you prefer later in the week, Thursday 08:30 PT works for me. Otherwise, Tuesday 09:00 PT is fine.

Attachments: kv-cache-seq-diagram.png (for reference)

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@nebulah.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@nebulah.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: deep dive on serving runtime for Nebula Health POC

Thanks, Stephanie and Jonas — appreciate the detail. Quick update from our side: an internal leadership sync popped up on Tue morning, so we need to move off the Tue 09:00 slot. Thu 08:30 PT looks good. Can we confirm Thu 2026-05-27 08:30–09:45 PT (we increased to 75 min to allow longer Q&A)?

Request: can the team add a 10-minute segment on quantization fallbacks and how Redwood handles per-model profile changes at runtime? Also, please include the mutual action plan / success criteria in the invite or a shared doc.

We'll try to include a short (anonymized) trace from one of our services before EOD Fri if possible. If not, I'll at least bring the sequence length distribution.

Best,
Alice
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Final: Redwood x Nebula Health — runtime deep dive (Thu 2026-05-27 08:30 PT)

Confirmed — Thu 27 May 2026 08:30–09:45 PT (75 min). Calendar invite sent (link below).

Updated agenda (final):
- 5 min — introductions & success criteria
- 20 min — runtime topology + kernel selection logic (Jonas)
- 15 min — KV cache design & sequence diagrams (Jonas)
- 10 min — quantization fallback strategies & per-model profiles (Rishi)
- 20–25 min — open Q&A, next steps, mutual action plan

Pre-reads attached and linked: ri-runtime-overview-v1.pdf (slides), kv-cache-seq-diagram.png, deepdive-agenda-v2.pdf. I've also added a Mutual Action Plan doc to the Drive folder — please review before the meeting: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRI-runtime-prereads

Calendar: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abcd1234-nebula-runtime-dive
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRI-runtime-prereads
Confluence notes (internal summary): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFR/DEAL-4521+Nebula+Health+Integration

Looking forward to it.

Thanks,

Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
